body: Watch the first three seconds with the sound off. If it doesn't grab you muted, it won't grab anyone — most first views are silent.
Watermark sweep: no TikTok logo, no CapCut outro, no bouncing username. Re-export clean or don't post.
Caption check: no clickable URL. 'Link in bio' in words is free; a pasted link costs reach.
Bait check: no 'tag a friend', no 'comment YES', no 'like if'. If the caption asks for mechanical engagement, rewrite it as a real question.
Would YOU send this to one specific person? Name them in your head. No name, weak post.
Is there something worth saving here — a lyric, a date, a chord, a list? One save-worthy element per post is the bar.
Read the caption out loud once. If it doesn't sound like you talking at the merch table, it's not done.
Posting window: Reels at 5–7pm MT weekdays, photos mid-morning. If it's ready at the wrong hour, schedule it — don't burn it.
Venue, collaborators, photographer — everyone in the frame or on the bill gets tagged. Tags are distribution.
On-screen text readable on a phone at arm's length? Big, high-contrast, off the bottom edge where the caption overlaps.
Cover frame check: does the thumbnail read at grid size? Your grid is the first thing a new listener judges.
If it's an original song, is the audio posted as its own named sound? Don't ship the clip without claiming the audio.
Location tag on. Denver and Front Range listeners are the ones who buy tickets — help the platform find them.
Show post? Facebook Event exists, venue tagged, date correct. The post promotes; the Event converts.
Cross-post plan: same clean file goes to Facebook natively. Posting the IG share-link to FB is a half-post.
First-hour plan: can you be near your phone for 45 minutes after posting? Replying in the first hour is part of the post.
If this is a reaction or commentary clip: is YOUR take actually in it? Bare reposts get demoted — your two cents makes it yours.
Date, time, venue, city — if any of these are in the post, triple-check them. A wrong show date is the one unrecoverable typo.
One post, one job. If it announces a show AND teases a song AND thanks a venue, split it into three posts.
Story plan: the post goes to Stories too, with the link sticker if there's anywhere to send people.
Vertical check for Reels: full 9:16, no letterboxing, nothing critical in the bottom third where UI covers it.
Audio level check: voice above guitar, guitar above room noise. One bad mix reads as amateur faster than any visual.
Does frame one start mid-action? Trim every second of setup — walking to the chair is not the hook.
Hashtags: 8–15, yours plus idea-specific, at the end of the caption or first comment — never woven into sentences.
If a person other than you is identifiable in the shot, did they say yes? Small towns, small scenes — ask.
Alt text on Feed photos: one sentence, what's actually in the picture. Accessibility and search in one thirty-second step.
Scroll your own last three posts first. If this one's the same shape as all three, vary the format — feeds reward variety within identity.
Merch or music mentioned? The bio link better actually point there today — a dead-end 'link in bio' burns trust.
Cover song check: title and original artist named in caption. Credit is legally smart and algorithmically read as context.
Is this the 4th+ Reel this week? Cadence target is 3–5 — bank this one for Monday instead of crowding Friday.
Battery, storage, and the take you almost deleted: before you leave any filming moment, shoot one extra take and one wide. Future posts live in the outtakes.
Last look at the whole thing as a stranger: would someone who's never heard of you know what you sound like from this post? If not, does it at least make them want to find out?
